$description: C Protocol Coverage Taxonomy — maps every Gold FN to a protocol category. Updated after each experiment.
$milestone: L1 Regex-Friendly categories cleared (Exp-018 through Exp-022)

capability_map.description: Which categories can be solved by regex-based detection, and which need deeper analysis?

regex_friendly.definition: Violation signal is visible in function call presence/absence. Cleanup vs. no cleanup. Validation vs. no validation.
regex_friendly.status: CLEARED — all L1 recoverable FNs resolved

regex_hostile.definition: Clean and violation functions have identical call signatures. Distinction requires control flow, data flow, or IR enhancement.
regex_hostile.note: These categories need CFG (L2), data flow analysis, or IR improvements (L4).

categories.name: Key Derivation Safety
categories.description: ECDH, Curve25519, DH, and key exchange functions must validate key types and clean up crypto material.

fns.note: Has EVP_PKEY_free + EC_KEY_get0_group. Gold violation differs from our category definition.
Has DH_free + BN_free. Gold violation differs from our category definition.
ssh_buffer_new without free. File-level context gives false credit.

categories.name: Auth Message Lifecycle
categories.description: NTLM, SPNEGO, and SSH userauth message construction. Clean and violation functions have identical call signatures — cannot be distinguished by regex alone.
categories.diagnosis: 5/5 recovered with no safeguards, but +11 FP. All auth functions (clean and violation) call FreeContextBuffer, ssh_pki_*, etc. Distinction requires control flow or data flow analysis.

fns.note: Trigger fires, but same call pattern as clean auth functions.
Trigger fires, but same call pattern as clean auth functions.
Trigger fires, but same call pattern as clean ssh_userauth_*.
Trigger fires, but same call pattern as clean ssh_userauth_*.
Trigger fires, but same call pattern as clean ssh_agent_*.

categories.name: TLS Configuration Safety
categories.description: TLS/Schannel configuration functions must validate certificates and handle errors.

fns.note: Likely regex_hostile — configure functions have similar call patterns.
Recovered via snake_case trigger (Exp-017 had net negative ROI overall).

categories.name: Connection Lifecycle Safety
categories.description: Connection functions must validate socket state and handle disconnection cleanup. Regex-friendly in theory, but single FN is a gold mismatch.

fns.note: Has CONN_SOCK_IDX_VALID. Gold violation is about something else.

categories.name: State Machine Transitions
categories.description: Protocol state machines must validate state transitions and handle error states. Regex-hostile: requires control flow analysis.

categories.name: Certificate Pinning Validation
categories.description: Certificate/public key pinning operations must verify certificate chains. Pin without X.509 verify is a clear gap.

fns.note: Pins pubkey without X509_verify_cert or SSL_get_verify_result.

categories.name: Safeguard Logic (False Match)
categories.description: Existing rules triggered but safeguards falsely matched. Fixed by tightening safeguard (removing standalone 'token|session'). Known tradeoff: +3 FP on same-file functions (triggered by 'getenv' via /i flag on [A-Z]).
categories.tradeoff: 3 new FPs on same-file config/connection functions. Net: +3 TP, +3 FP. Trigger [A-Z]+/i root cause identified, fix deferred (would break 10 curl TPs).

categories.name: Macro-Defined Callbacks
categories.description: C macro-defined packet callbacks lack IR-level visibility. Regex-hostile: requires IR enhancement.

aggregate.milestone: L1 (Regex-Friendly) categories CLEARED. Remaining 2 FNs require L2-L4 capabilities.
aggregate.note: 7/19 recovered (37% overall). Of 10 actionable FNs (excl. gold_mismatch, regex_saturated, deferred), 7 recovered = 70%. Remaining: state_machine (L4), tls_config/mbed_configure_ssl (L2). Regex-friendly coverage = 5/5 = 100% of solvable L1 FNs.
